title: SQL for DS interviews | Transformers & tokenization
objectives: Write window-function SQL fluently under time pressure. Explain self-attention and tokenization from first principles.
exercise: Solve 8 timed SQL problems (25 min each) covering retention, funnel, rolling metric and top-N per group. Then implement single-head attention in NumPy and check output shapes.
resources: Interview Query / DataLemur-style SQL banks (practise in your Week 1 DuckDB setup)
Karpathy: Let's build GPT: from scratch, in code, spelled out
Karpathy: Let's build the GPT Tokenizer
Stanford CME 295 Transformers & LLMs (lectures free on YouTube)

units.title: Tokenization & BPE
units.concepts: Subword tokens, byte-pair encoding, token economics

cards.q: What is the difference between RANK and DENSE_RANK on ties?
choices: RANK leaves gaps after ties (1,1,3); DENSE_RANK doesn't (1,1,2)

cards.q: Amounts ordered DESC: 100, 100, 90. What does DENSE_RANK() return for the 90 row?
Why does WHERE ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...) <= 3 fail?
choices: Window functions are evaluated after WHERE; filter in an outer query/CTE or use QUALIFY
ROW_NUMBER needs an ORDER BY in the outer query

cards.q: LAG(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) returns…
choices: The same user's previous transaction amount (NULL for their first)
The previous row in the whole table

cards.q: Top 3 merchants by revenue in each city. Which pattern?
choices: CTE with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY revenue DESC), then filter rn <= 3
cards.explain: Use RANK instead if ties should all be included.

cards.q: Frame clause for a 7-day trailing sum over a table with exactly one row per day?
choices: ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 6 FOLLOWING
cards.explain: 6 preceding plus the current row = 7 rows.

cards.q: Why join to a date spine before a ROWS-based rolling window?
choices: Missing days would make '6 PRECEDING' rows span more than 7 calendar days
cards.explain: Alternatively, use RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL 6 DAY PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW where supported.

cards.q: Why can't WAU be computed by summing the last 7 days of DAU?
choices: Users active on several days are double-counted; you need COUNT(DISTINCT user) over the 7-day span
It can; that's the standard method

cards.q: DAU = 200k, MAU = 1M. What is the DAU/MAU 'stickiness' ratio? (decimal)
cards.explain: On average, users are active about 6 days a month.

cards.q: A common way to compute a rolling 7-day distinct-user count in SQL?
choices: Self-join the date spine to activity on activity_date BETWEEN d − 6 AND d, then COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) GROUP BY d
cards.explain: Most engines don't support COUNT(DISTINCT) as a window function.

cards.q: Spot the bug: a Day-N retention query divides 'users active on day N' by 'users active on day N'.
choices: The denominator must be the cohort size (users who started on day 0)
cards.explain: Retention = active on day N / cohort size.

cards.q: Order the steps of a cohort retention query.
items: Find each user's first activity date (cohort)
Count distinct users per cohort × day N

cards.q: Your D30 retention chart shows the most recent cohorts collapsing. Most likely cause?
choices: Those cohorts haven't reached day 30 yet (right-censoring); exclude immature cohorts

cards.q: 'Classic' Day-7 retention vs 'unbounded' (rolling) Day-7 retention?
choices: Classic: active exactly on day 7; unbounded: active on day 7 or any later day
Classic counts sessions; unbounded counts users

cards.q: A cohort has 2,000 users; 500 are active on day 7. D7 retention in %?
How do you keep only each user's first event per day?
choices: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, DATE(ts) ORDER BY ts) = 1

cards.q: In an ordered funnel (view → add_to_cart → pay), the join condition for step 2 must include…
Client retries create duplicate 'payment_success' rows. Best dedup key?
cards.explain: Distinct payments by the same user in the same minute are real.

cards.q: Funnel: 10,000 views → 3,000 add-to-cart → 1,200 payments. Overall view-to-pay conversion in %?
Spot the bug: FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id WHERE o.status = 'paid'
choices: The WHERE filter on the right table drops unmatched users, turning it into an inner join; move the condition into ON
LEFT JOIN should be RIGHT JOIN

cards.q: Why do LLMs struggle to count letters in a word?
cards.answer: They see subword tokens, not characters. 'strawberry' may be 2–3 tokens, so letter-level structure isn't directly visible and must be inferred from learned associations.
rubric: Input is subword tokens, not characters
Character info is implicit / not directly observed

cards.q: How does BPE build its vocabulary?
choices: Start from bytes/characters and repeatedly merge the most frequent adjacent pair
Use a dictionary of English words

cards.q: Why does the same sentence often cost more tokens in Thai or Bahasa than in English?
choices: The tokenizer was trained mostly on English, so other languages split into more, shorter tokens
cards.explain: More tokens means higher cost, more latency and less effective context.

cards.q: Rough rule of thumb for English text?
Main advantage of byte-level BPE?
choices: Any string can be encoded: no unknown tokens

cards.q: Why divide QKᵀ by √d_k?
choices: Dot-product variance grows with d_k; unscaled scores saturate the softmax and shrink gradients

cards.q: Scaled dot-product attention is…
d_model = 512 with 8 heads. What is the per-head dimension d_k?
For a sequence of length T, what is the shape of one head's attention weight matrix?
cards.explain: This is the source of the O(T²) cost.

cards.q: Why use multiple heads instead of one big head?
choices: Each head can attend to different relations/subspaces in parallel at similar total cost
To make attention linear in T

cards.q: What does the causal mask prevent during training?
choices: Positions attending to future tokens, which would leak the answer for next-token prediction

cards.q: How is the causal mask usually applied?
choices: Set scores above the diagonal to −∞ before the softmax
Multiply V by a lower-triangular matrix after softmax
Drop future tokens from the batch
Zero the gradients of future tokens

cards.q: What does RoPE do?
choices: Rotates Q and K by position-dependent angles so their dot product depends on relative position
Adds learned absolute position vectors to V

cards.q: Why do transformer blocks use residual connections (x + f(x))?
choices: They keep a clean gradient path through deep stacks; each block learns an update

cards.q: Greedy decoding…
choices: Picks the highest-probability token at each step
Picks a random token from the top-p set

cards.q: What grows with context length in the KV cache, and why does it matter for serving cost?
cards.answer: For each past token, every layer stores its key and value vectors. So memory grows linearly with context length (× batch × layers × KV heads × head dim). GPU memory then caps how many concurrent requests fit, and decode is memory-bandwidth bound. Long contexts mean fewer users per GPU and higher cost per token.
rubric: Stored K and V per token per layer
Limits concurrency / memory-bandwidth bound decode → cost

cards.q: What does the KV cache avoid?
choices: Recomputing keys and values for all previous tokens at every decoding step

cards.q: KV cache per token = 2 (K,V) × layers × KV heads × head_dim × bytes. For 32 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, fp16 (2 bytes): how many KiB per token?
cards.explain: 2·32·8·128·2 = 131,072 bytes = 128 KiB. A 32k context is therefore ≈ 4 GiB per sequence.

cards.q: Grouped-query attention (GQA) cuts KV-cache memory by…
choices: Sharing each K/V head across several query heads

cards.q: Prefill vs decode phases of LLM inference?
choices: Prefill processes the prompt in parallel (compute-bound); decode emits one token at a time (memory-bandwidth-bound)
Prefill is slower per token than decode
